The virtual assistant does not require this data for processing.
Can the virtual assistant access my data?

It is an artificial intelligence-based chatbot. It can automatically answer questions about official matters. It uses large language models such as PLLuM and Llama 3.3. Its knowledge comes from information available on official state websites. These include:

- info.mobywatel.gov.pl,
- descriptions of selected services on the gov.pl website,
- websites of ministries on the gov.pl website,
- prezydent.pl.

Ask it your questions as though you were talking to a human assistant. For example:

- How do I sign a document electronically?
- How can I get a copy of a birth certificate?
- When should I apply for care allowance?
- How can I check whether my ID card has been suspended?
- What to do to enrol my child in a nursery on-line?
- Where can I check my passport details?

In order to provide the most accurate answers, the assistant may ask you some follow-up questions.
How to use the virtual assistant?

A Large Language Model (LLM) is an advanced artificial intelligence system. It can understand and create content in natural language, that is the language used by humans. It was trained on a huge number of texts, including articles, books and websites. The language model is neither sentient nor knowledgeable in the conventional sense. It uses linguistic patterns inferred from the texts it was trained on to answer questions.
What is a large language model?

A virtual assistant can help you find information on official matters. It is still in the testing stage, so it may occasionally provide inaccurate or incorrect answers. Some of its answers may sound convincing, yet still contain incorrect information.\nTherefore, it is advisable to approach the virtual assistant\'s answers critically and verify them using other sources.

Your ID card with an electronic layer may have:

• An attendance certificate that allows you to confirm your presence at a given place and time.

• An identification and authentication certificate that lets you log in to government websites using your personal profile.

• A personal signature certificate, which enables electronic signing of documents using a personal signature. You can use it, for example, in the Personal signature service in the mObywatel app.

• A qualified signature certificate (not visible in the mObywatel application) – which enables electronic signing of documents using a qualified signature. You can purchase this certificate from a qualified service provider.

ID card certificates can have the following statuses in the mObywatel application:

• Active – this means that you have this certificate stored electronically on your ID card and have activated it. Some certificates, for example of a personal signature, will be active if you set a PIN for them at the office when collecting your ID card. The attendance certificate will be activated as soon as your ID card has been issued.

• Inactive – this means that you have this certificate in the electronic layer of your ID card, but you cannot use it. This happens when the certificate requires a PIN that you have not established at the office.

• None – means you do not have this certificate. You will receive a personal signature certificate when you apply for a new ID card and indicate that you want the ID card to have this certificate embedded.

• Blocked – means that this certificate is uploaded to the electronic layer of your ID card, but has been blocked. This will happen when, for example, you sign a document in an app or change the PIN for a certificate and enter the wrong PIN three times.
